analysis: Changed behavior: LaunchAgent.kickstartInPlace (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/LaunchAgent.swift, head ~196-217) now returns Bool. With reloadIfMissing=false (watchdog path via kickstartIfLoaded), a 'could not find service' result (exit 113, '3:' or case-insensitive text) returns false instead of true. Previously the watchdog was told a restart happened when the job had vanished. With reloadIfMissing=true, it reloads via loadService and returns true. This tightens the control that the watchdog must not resurrect a user-stopped provider (relates to T-043, TB-003 watchdog authority). The restart() caller at base line 152 discards the result via @discardableResult. No new privilege, no new unauthenticated surface, and no change to attestation, encryption or key handling. The docs change (installation.md head 217-223) describes this behavior. Remaining risks: the match on stderr.contains("3:") is loose and could misclassify an unrelated error as 'service not found'. That would be a false 'no restart' rather than a security issue. WatchdogRecoveryService.recoverDownProvider and the guard rollback it references are not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that it handles the false return and rolls back the staged crash-loop backend guard. Nothing in this diff covers that. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the supplied changes.
